name: rule-judge-exam
title: A model judging rule proposals for the person

conditions.sample: 56 rule proposals from the author's archive, each labelled by the person as one they would keep or not
conditions.source: the author's own session archive; only counts leave it
conditions.judges: Haiku and Sonnet with the proposal alone; Opus also given the person's global instructions and the project's rules in force
conditions.verdicts: serve, covered (already said by a rule or the global instructions), setup (about one session or period) or not

summary: Whether a model can decide rule proposals on the person's behalf, since in practice nobody reviews the queue: 84 proposals were waiting.

metrics.label: Tentative rules as built, kept by the person
metrics.note: served on repeats alone, with no model deciding

metrics.label: Haiku, no context: served rules the person keeps
Sonnet, no context: served rules the person keeps
Opus with global instructions and project rules: agrees with the person
Opus with context: served, and kept by the person
Opus with context: dismissed as already covered, though the person called them true

bar: at least 90% of served rules kept
meaning: Automatic adding stays imperfect, so ctx's automatic judge leans toward deleting: most proposals it dismisses, often as already covered, and every decision, kept or dismissed, is shown at session start, in ctx rules activity and on the decisions page, and reversible with ctx rules undo.
